history.prompt:
Create an original publication-quality technical explanatory illustration as a no-text PNG. The supplied external images are mechanism references only: independently design a fresh composition, never imitate their layout or typography. Use a pure white canvas (transparent is acceptable only if it composites as pure white), thin muted graphite flow arrows, flat 2D orthographic shapes, smooth solid pale fills. Palette: cyan input (#4DBBD5), green processing (#00A087), warm orange pooling (#F39B7F), muted blue representations (#3C5488), red output/gradients (#E64B35), neutral gray supporting parts. Colors at low opacity for large areas, stronger outlines and small accents. Balance white modules with selectively pale colored groups, one dominant color per semantic group. Same semantic modules share treatment; adjacent unlike semantics have different color. No glossy icon tiles, no card dashboard, no thick title bars, no decorative 3D, no perspective side faces, no extruded tensors, no shadow, glow, blur, gradient, texture, paper grain, noise, ripple, stripe or watermark. Mechanism marks (flat grids, feature-map thumbnails, small nodes, pooling cells) must carry scientific information rather than decorative icons. Optional decorative icons at most one per group; preferably none for operator diagrams. Avoid excessive boxes around everything. Reserve generous blank title and adjacent numeric annotation areas for later real-font typesetting. ABSOLUTELY NO readable text, letters, digits, equations, operation symbols, pseudo-glyphs, placeholder scribbles or watermark. All labels and math will be added later. A handwritten specimen inside an input image is an allowed visual sample, not a printed label. Arrowheads are required at actual destinations, no disconnected stubs or unexplained edges.

Scientific brief:
Explain original historical LeNet-5 on handwritten gray digit image, with EIGHT stage groups along left-to-right sequence: input; first convolution; first learned subsampling; second convolution; second learned subsampling; third convolution; dense layer; RBF distance readout. Correct sizes and labels will be typeset later. Feature maps as FLAT FRONT-VIEW miniature grayscale digit silhouettes or grids arranged with small offsets without 3D side faces. Convolution groups green and learned-subsampling groups pale orange; they alternate. Show an informative small 5-by-5 kernel inset in each convolution group and a 2-by-2 cell reduction inset in each subsampling group, with blank operation label areas below. Learned subsampling is trainable scaling+bias after local averaging, NOT max pooling; show a small compact scale control motif with no symbols. Second convolution uses selective rather than fully dense channel connectivity; avoid misleading all-to-all detailed drawing there. Final RBF outputs are distance/prototype comparisons, not softmax bars. Use one input handwritten zero specimen only as image content; no printed digits. End dense/RBF groups with node columns and prototype-distance curves, not an empty generic box. Rich mechanism content but visually light, no icon tile headings or uniform cards. Leave blank top heading and dimension line and bottom operation detail line for each stage.

Revise THIS fresh LeNet-5 draft only. Preserve rich eight-stage main path, handwritten specimen and learned subsampling and RBF readout. Correct each green convolution detail grid beneath C1, C3 and C5: each MUST have exactly FIVE rows and FIVE columns of cells (5x5), not four. Both orange learned-subsampling mini-grids remain TWO rows by TWO columns. C5 main feature group should be small feature coordinate rectangles/vectors rather than another spatial handwritten-image stack, because spatial extent is one-by-one: retain rich128-ish illustrative width without printing numbers. No operator titles, labels, letters or numbers. Make all fill regions smooth pale flat solid, no grain/gradient/shadows.

Edit ONLY this newly generated no-text LeNet diagram background. There are unwanted faint gray pseudo-writing/scribble fragments OUTSIDE the panel title strips: above the colored top header boxes and below the dimension footer boxes. REMOVE ALL these ghost words completely, leaving those surrounding areas pure white/transparent blank. No replacement text or marks. Do not generate ANY letters/digits/labels/pseudo-text. Keep handwritten zero specimen inside input image. Green kernel grid icons may remain schematic cropped small arrays, not literal full count. Preserve all stage boxes, learned-subsampling2x2 mechanisms, RBF readout, arrow directions and positions. C5 spatial extent is1x1: replace its large spatial handwritten-map stack by multiple small flat scalar coordinate tiles (not cropped spatial zero images). They represent a channel vector, not spatial feature maps. Do not alter any other objects. Flat uniform pale fills, no glow/shadow/gradient/texture.

Edit ONLY the C5 green panel, the sixth panel from the left, of this freshly generated no-text LeNet draft. Every other panel, arrow, canvas dimension, blank text strip and color stays identical. C5 output has spatial size ONE BY ONE and 120 channels. DELETE COMPLETELY its stack of large handwritten-zero feature maps and the green dashed receptive-field arrows currently pointing at them. Do not replace them by any spatial zero images. In the SAME upper-middle region of C5, draw a modest horizontal group of small FLAT SQUARE coordinate tiles, all front-facing and identical size, with a few more tiles below if necessary. These tiles are channel coordinates, with no image content inside; just pale green solid squares with thin darker green outlines and a tiny neutral ellipsis to show omitted channels. Keep the separate schematic kernel-grid motif at bottom of C5 to illustrate its convolution. No text, digits, formula, labels or pseudo-words. Pure white or transparent canvas, uniform pale fills, absolutely no gradients/shadows/ripple/texture/3D.
